title: The Story of the Slave-Girl Anis al-Jalis and Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Khaqan

paragraphs.en: In Basra once reigned King Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman al-Zainabi, known for his generosity and popularity. He was like a bountiful sea, making even proud men serve him willingly. His viziers were Fadl al-Din ibn-Khaqan and al-Mu'in ibn-Sawi.
paragraphs.zh: 在巴士拉曾经统治着穆罕默德·本-苏莱曼·扎伊纳比国王，他以慷慨和受欢迎著称。他就像一片丰饶的海洋，连骄傲的人都甘愿为他效劳。他的宰相是法尔兹丁·本-哈赞和穆因·本-萨瓦伊。

paragraphs.en: Fadl al-Din was renowned for his kindness and noble conduct, loved by all, especially women who wished he would live long. In contrast, al-Mu'in was the most greedy and vicious man of his time, cunning as a fox and cruel as a dog.
paragraphs.zh: 法尔德丁以仁慈和高尚的行为著称，深受所有人喜爱，尤其是那些希望他长命百岁的女性。相比之下，阿穆因则是当时最贪婪、最恶毒的人，狡猾如狐，残忍如狼。

paragraphs.en: Fadl al-Din's virtues were celebrated in verse: "A noble and godly man / Who helps a friend and thereby pleases life." No one could turn away from him without finding relief. Al-Mu'in, however, was despised for his wickedness: "A mean and wretched infidel / Who preys on everyone who comes and goes."
paragraphs.zh: 法尔德丁的美德被赞颂在诗中：“一位高贵而虔诚的人/帮助朋友，因此让生活变得美好。”没有人能远离他而不感到轻松。然而，阿勒穆因因其邪恶而备受鄙视：“一个卑劣而可悲的异教徒/掠夺来来往往的所有人。”

paragraphs.en: The people's love for Fadl al-Din matched their hatred of al-Mu'in.
paragraphs.zh: 人们的爱戴之情与对阿穆因的憎恨不相上下。

paragraphs.en: As King Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman al-Zainabi sat on his throne, he ordered Fadl ibn-Khaqan to find a slave-girl of unparalleled beauty, wisdom, and grace. His courtiers estimated the cost at ten thousand dinars. The king instructed his treasurer to provide this sum to Fadl.
paragraphs.zh: 穆罕默德·本-萨利曼·扎伊纳比国王坐在王座上，命令法德尔·本-哈卡恩寻找一位无与伦比的美丽、智慧和优雅的女奴。他的朝臣估计所需费用为一万第纳尔。国王吩咐财政大臣拨出这笔款项交给法德尔。

paragraphs.en: The vizier employed brokers to scout the market daily for such a girl. One day, a broker approached him with a young woman who met the king's criteria. She was five feet tall, slender-waisted, and had heavy hips and swelling breasts.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 派了一批经纪人每天在市场搜寻符合条件的女奴。有一天，一个经纪人带来了一位年轻女子，她符合国王的标准。这位女子身高五英尺左右，腰肢纤细，臀部丰满，胸部也颇为挺拔。

paragraphs.en: Her face was smooth, her eyes black, and she exuded an elegance surpassing that of a bending bough.
paragraphs.zh: 她的脸庞光滑细腻，眼睛乌黑明亮，浑身散发着超越柔韧枝条的优雅气质。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad spoke to King Muhammad:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹尔对穆罕默德王说道：

paragraphs.en: I heard that none pleased the vizier until a broker brought him a girl who was as lovely as the moon, excelling in beauty even antelopes and deer. The Glorious God had bestowed upon her honor, fame, virtue, and all graces. Seven stars guarded her cheeks, ensuring no one could steal a glance at her.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，直到一个经纪人带来一位如同明月般美丽的女奴后，才让 vizier 马上满意。这位女子的美貌远超羚羊和鹿。荣耀之神赐予她荣誉、名声、美德以及所有恩宠。她的脸颊两侧有七颗守护之星，确保无人能一窥她的容颜。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad shot Anis al-Jalis with a falling star. The vizier was delighted, asking the broker about her price. The broker replied that she cost ten thousand dinars and had learned much, including grammar, jurisprudence, medicine, and music.
paragraphs.zh: 沙弗拉扎德的目光如流星般落在安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯身上， vizier 见状喜上眉梢，连忙询问经纪人她的价格。经纪人回答说她价值一万第纳尔，并且学识渊博，涉猎了语法、法学、医学和音乐等多个领域。

paragraphs.en: The vizier summoned Anis's old Persian master, who appeared frail and decrepit. The vizier offered him ten thousand dinars for Anis, to which the man agreed without hesitation.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 召见了安尼斯的老波斯主人，那人显得瘦弱苍老。vizier 提出以一万第纳尔的价格买下安尼斯，对方毫不犹豫地答应了。

paragraphs.en: With the money in hand, the vizier turned back to the broker.
paragraphs.zh: 拿着钱，首相转身对上了那位经纪人。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad was interrupted by dawn, but Dinarzad praised her sister's story. Shahrazad promised an even better tale if she survived another night with King Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman al-Zainabi.
paragraphs.zh: 天边已泛起鱼肚白，莎赫拉兹德的话被打断了，但丁尔扎德还是称赞了姐姐的故事。莎赫拉兹德向国王穆罕默德·本-萨利曼·齐纳比许诺，如果她能再陪国王度过一个夜晚，她将讲述一个更加精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began anew.
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹adin接着讲起了她的故事。

paragraphs.en: The broker approached the vizier, suggesting he keep the slave-girl Anis al-Jalis for fifteen days before presenting her to King Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman al-Zainabi. The girl had just arrived from a journey and needed time to recover. Following this advice, the vizier took the girl to his palace, placed her in a private chamber, and provided her with generous daily provisions of chickens, wine, and fine clothes.
paragraphs.zh: 经纪人走近首相，建议他先让奴隶女孩安妮斯·阿尔吉拉斯待十五天，然后再呈献给穆罕默德·本-萨利曼·扎伊纳比国王。这个女孩刚从旅途归来，需要时间恢复体力。遵照这一建议，首相将女孩带回了自己的宫殿，安置在一间私密的房间内，并为她提供了丰盛的日用品，包括鸡肉、葡萄酒和精致的衣服。

paragraphs.en: The vizier also had a son, described as fair and graceful, with rosy cheeks and a mole like ambergris. A poet had praised him, comparing him to a charming moon and a captivating bough. The young man was unaware of the girl's presence, but his father warned her about his dangerous nature.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 也有一个儿子，相貌英俊，举止优雅，脸颊红润，身上还有一颗像琥珀色的痣。一位诗人曾赞美过他，将他比作迷人皓月和令人着迷的枝条。年轻人对此毫不知情，但他的父亲警告她，要小心这个危险的人物。

paragraphs.en: The vizier instructed Anis al-Jalis to guard against his son and avoid any contact with him. She agreed, "I hear and obey," before he left.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 嘱咐安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯女奴要防备自己的儿子，避免与他有任何接触。她应道：“我听命遵行”，随后他就离开了。

paragraphs.en: A few days later, Anis al-Jalis went to the palace bath. One of the maids washed her, enhancing her beauty. Afterward, she was dressed in youthful attire and greeted the vizier’s wife with a kiss.
paragraphs.zh: 几天后，安伊斯·阿吉勒斯去了王宫浴室。一名侍女为她沐浴并精心打扮，更突显了她的美丽。随后，她换上了青春洋溢的服饰，并亲吻了首相夫人的脸颊，迎接她的到来。

paragraphs.en: The lady said, "May the bath bring you blessings." Anis replied, "May God send you all joy."
paragraphs.zh: 女士说：“愿沐浴给你带来祝福。”安伊斯回答道：“但愿上帝赐你一切快乐。”

paragraphs.en: The lady asked, "How did you find the bath?" Anis responded, "It is fine; just right at this moment, lacking only your presence." The lady then invited her waiting women to join her for a bath.
paragraphs.zh: 女士问道：“你洗澡怎么样？”安伊斯回答说：“还不错，就差你一个人没来。”随后，女士邀请她的侍女们一起来沐浴。

paragraphs.en: They agreed and went together.
paragraphs.zh: 他们达成一致，便一同出发了。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Anis al-Jalis returned to her chamber with two maids instructed by the vizier’s wife to guard the door.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，安伊斯·阿吉勒斯返回了自己的房间，两名女仆在首相夫人指示下守在门口警戒。

paragraphs.en: Later, Nur al-Din Ali entered his mother's apartment. Seeing the two maids at the door, he asked about his mother. The story ended as Shahrazad paused, promising a more entertaining tale the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 后来，努尔·丁·阿里走进了母亲的房间。看到门口站着两个女仆，他询问起母亲的情况。故事在沙赫拉兹阿德暂停时结束了，她承诺如果自己能活到第二天晚上，将会讲述一个更加有趣的故事。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that Nur al-Din asked the two maids about his mother, who had gone to the bath. Anis al-Jalis wondered if she was the young man they warned her about. She ran from the bath, looked at Nur al-Din, and sighed when he appeared as radiant as the full moon.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，努尔·阿丁询问了两位侍女关于他母亲的消息，他的母亲去了澡堂。安伊斯·阿尔吉里斯怀疑那是否就是她们警告她注意的那个年轻人。她从澡堂中跑了出来，看到努尔·阿丁出现在眼前，不禁轻叹了一声，只见他光彩照人，犹如满月一般。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din turned and saw Anis al-Jalis; both sighed in unison, falling into love. He approached the two maids, who fled in fear. Then, he went to Anis al-Jalis's door, entered, and asked if she was the girl his father bought for him.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁转过身来，看见了奴隶女孩安伊斯·阿勒吉利斯；两人不约而同地叹了口气，彼此坠入了爱河。他走近那两名侍女，她们吓得四处逃散。随后，他来到安伊斯·阿勒吉利斯的门前，推开门问道，是否就是他父亲为他买下的那个女孩。

paragraphs.en: She confirmed it.
paragraphs.zh: 她点了点头。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din, drunk with desire, pressed her legs against his sides while she wrapped her arms around his neck, giving him passionate kisses. He quickly undressed her and took her virginity. The two maids cried out in shock as Nur al-Din fled the scene, fearing the consequences of his actions.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁被欲望冲昏了头脑，将腿紧贴在他的侧身，双臂环绕住他的脖子，给予他充满激情的吻。他迅速脱去她的衣物，夺去了她的童贞。两名侍女惊呼一声，目瞪口呆地望着努尔·阿丁仓皇逃走，生怕自己的行为会带来不良后果。

paragraphs.en: When the vizier’s wife heard cries, she rushed from her bath to see what was happening. She found two maids trembling and said, "What is wrong?" They replied that Nur al-Din had beaten them before entering Anis al-Jalis's room, where he embraced her for a while but left in haste.
paragraphs.zh: 当 vizier 的妻子听到哭喊声时，她匆匆从浴室出来查看发生了什么。她发现两个女仆在发抖，问道：“怎么了？”女仆们回答说，Nur al-Din 在进入 Anis al-Jalis 的房间之前已经打了她们一顿，随后他抱了一会儿 Anis al-Jalis，但很快就离开了。

paragraphs.en: The vizier’s wife entered Anis al-Jalis's chamber and asked what had happened. Anis al-Jalis recounted how a young man suddenly appeared, claiming to be the son of her master who had bought her. She admitted that she thought it was true until he embraced her.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 的妻子走进安伊斯·阿尔贾利斯的房间，问发生了什么事。安伊斯·阿尔贾利斯讲述了事情经过：一个年轻人突然出现，声称自己是她主人的儿子，并且她的主人正是买下她的那个人。她说起初她还信以为真，直到对方拥抱了她。

paragraphs.en: The vizier’s wife then inquired if Nur al-Din had done "you-know-what" and learned that he did so three times.
paragraphs.zh: 随后， vizier 的妻子询问 Nur al-Din 是否做了“你知道的那些事”，得知他一共做了三次。

paragraphs.en: The vizier's wife feared for their safety, saying, "I hope you won't have to pay the price!" She and the maids wept, fearing Nur al-Din’s father might punish him severely.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 的妻子担心他们的安危，说道：“但愿你不必付出代价！”她和女仆们流下了眼泪，害怕 Nur al-Din 的父亲会严厉惩罚他。

paragraphs.en: Before they could explain further, the vizier entered. Nobody dared tell him what had occurred. He approached his wife instead.
paragraphs.zh: 还没等他们解释清楚，首相进来了。没有人敢告诉他发生了什么。他径直走向了妻子。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad remarked on the story's strangeness, to which Shahrazad replied that it was nothing compared to what she would share the next night if she lived.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默不作声。丁纳札德对这个故事感到有些诧异，沙赫拉兹德则回应说，这比起她若能活到明天晚上将要讲述的内容来说，简直微不足道。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the vizier approached his wife and demanded, "Tell me the truth." She replied, "Swear to do whatever I say first." He agreed.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，宰相走近他的妻子，问道：“告诉我真相。”她回答说：“你先答应做到我说的任何事。”他应允了。

paragraphs.en: She then revealed, "Your son went into Anis al-Jalis and took her virginity."
paragraphs.zh: 她随后说道：“你的儿子闯入了安妮丝·阿吉勒斯，并夺去了她的童贞。”

paragraphs.en: The vizier fell to the ground, beating his face until blood flowed from his nose and pulling out his beard. His wife pleaded, "My lord, you are harming yourself. I will give you ten thousand dinars for the girl."
paragraphs.zh: vizier 坠倒在地，用手捶打自己的脸，鲜血从鼻孔中流出，还拔出了胡须。他的妻子恳求道：“大人，您这是自作自受。我可以给您一万第纳尔买下这个女孩。”

paragraphs.en: But he replied, "I don’t need her price; I fear losing both my life and possessions."
paragraphs.zh: 但他回答说：“我不需要她的价格；我害怕连性命和财产都会失去。”

paragraphs.en: She asked, "How so?" He explained, "Our enemy al-Mu'in ibn-Sawi is waiting to exploit this. If he learns of it, he will tell the king that you bought a girl and took her virginity."
paragraphs.zh: 她问道：“怎么会这样？”他解释说：“我们的敌人阿慕因·本·萨维正在等着趁机作梗。如果他知道这件事，就会禀告国王你买了一个女孩并侵犯了她的童贞。”

paragraphs.en: The vizier continued, "The king will demand proof, I must bring Anis al-Jalis here. When questioned, she cannot deny what happened."
paragraphs.zh: 首相接着说：“国王一定会要求证据，我必须把安妮丝·阿吉勒斯带到这里来。一旦被问及，她无法否认发生的事情。”

paragraphs.en: His wife suggested, "Commit yourself to God; He will protect us from discovery." The vizier calmed down and drank a cup of wine.
paragraphs.zh: 他的妻子建议：“归依上帝吧，他会保护我们不被发现。”首相冷静下来，喝了一杯酒。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din avoided his father for a month, spending nights in the gardens. His mother urged his father to confront him, fearing he might run away. The vizier agreed to wait until Nur al-Din returned late one night.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿德丁一个月都没见父亲，晚上常在花园里度过。他母亲催促父亲找他谈谈，担心他会逃跑。首相同意等努尔·阿德丁深夜归来时再与他会面。

paragraphs.en: When Nur al-Din knocked on the door, his father hid and waited. As the young man entered, his father seized him, throwing him down. The mother intervened, asking why he intended to kill him.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁敲门时，他父亲躲了起来，静静地等待。年轻人进来后，他父亲突然冲上前，一把将他按倒在地。母亲赶紧出面干预，询问他为什么要杀掉自己的儿子。

paragraphs.en: The father, moved by emotion, knelt beside his son, revealing his intention to kill.
paragraphs.zh: 父亲情感激动，跪在儿子身旁，显露了他要杀掉儿子的意图。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din pleaded for mercy, quoting a poem: "Pardon my crime, for every mighty judge / Is used to mercy some offenders show. / I stand before you, guilty of all sins, / But you the ways of grace and mercy know."
paragraphs.zh: 奴仆女孩安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯和努尔丁·阿里·本-哈卡恩的故事 努尔丁求情，引用了一首诗：“宽恕我的罪行吧，每个伟大的法官/都会对一些犯错者施以仁慈。/我站在你面前，所有的罪孽都归于我，/但你却懂得恩典与宽容之道。”

paragraphs.en: The vizier felt compassion for his son Nur al-Din after hearing a verse about forgiveness. Nur al-Din kissed his father’s hands and feet, and his father said, "If I knew you would treat Anis al-Jalis fairly, I would give her to you." Nur al-Din promised not to take another wife or abuse her.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 听完一首关于宽恕的诗后，对儿子 Nur al-Din 产生了怜悯之情。Nur al-Din 亲吻了父亲的手和脚，父亲说道：“如果你能公平地对待 Anis al-Jalis，我愿意将她给你。”Nur al-Din 承诺不会另娶妻室或虐待她。

paragraphs.en: For a year, Nur al-Din lived happily with Anis al-Jalis. Meanwhile, the king forgot about the slave-girl. Al-Mu'in ibn-Sawi could not speak of the matter due to his close relationship with the vizier Fadl al-Din.
paragraphs.zh: 奴婢安伊斯·阿吉勒斯的女主人努尔·丁与她一起生活了一年，过得非常愉快。与此同时，国王早已将这位奴婢的事抛诸脑后。萨瓦伊·穆因因为与首相法德尔·丁关系密切，不便谈及此事。

paragraphs.en: One day, after catching a chill from the bath, Fadl al-Din fell ill and lay in bed. He wept, telling Nur al-Din that life is fleeting and everyone must die. His only advice was for Nur al-Din to fear God, weigh his actions, and care for Anis al-Jalis.
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，法尔德丁从浴室受了凉，一病不起，躺在床上。他泪流满面地对努尔丁说，人生苦短，终有一别。唯一叮嘱的是，努尔丁要敬畏上帝，慎重行事，并好好照顾安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din praised his father's good deeds. Fadl al-Din prayed for acceptance before dying. The household women cried loudly in the palace.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁称赞父亲的善行。法德丁祈祷后去世，宫中的女眷在大厅里哭声震天。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing of Fadl al-Din’s death, the king and citizens mourned deeply. Nur al-Din prepared his father for burial with great care. All attended the funeral, led by princes, viziers, and officers.
paragraphs.zh: 听到法尔德丁去世的消息，国王和百姓都极为悲痛。努尔丁精心准备了父亲的葬礼。所有官员、王子以及宰相都参加了这场葬礼。

paragraphs.en: A poet mourned him with verses.
paragraphs.zh: 一位诗人用诗句为他哀悼。

paragraphs.en: On Thursday night, after his father's burial, Nur al-Din returned home with his family and friends, still grieving deeply. One day, morning came, and Shahrazad paused her story.
paragraphs.zh: 在父亲安葬后的星期四晚上，努尔·阿尔丁与家人和朋友一同返回家中，依然沉浸在深深的悲痛中。一天清晨来临，沙赫拉兹德暂停了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that one day as the vizier’s son Nur al-Din sat in his father's palace, there was a knock at the door. He rose and opened it to find one of his father’s friends who kissed his hand and said, "My lord, he who has left the like of you is not dead. My lord Nur al-Din Ali, take comfort, be cheerful, and stop mourning."
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，有一天 vizier 的儿子努尔·阿丁坐在父亲的宫殿里时，有人敲门。他起身开门，发现是自己父亲的一位朋友，那人向他行礼并说道：“我的主啊，像您这样的人离开后，并未死去。我的主努尔·阿丁·阿里，请振作起来，开心一些，不要悲伤了。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din listened but continued to mourn for a long time. One day, his steward approached him with concern. "My lord Nur al-Din," the steward said, "have you not heard the saying 'He who spends without reckoning becomes poor without knowing it'?
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁听了却没有立即回应，而是继续沉浸在悲伤中。过了好一会儿，管家带着关切的神情走过来。“主人努尔丁啊，”管家说道，“你可曾听过‘不计后果地挥霍最终会不知穷困’这句谚语？”

paragraphs.en: My lord, this enormous expense and lavish giving will erode even mountains."
paragraphs.zh: 我的 Lord，如此巨大的开销和奢侈的施舍，终将侵蚀连山川也会动摇。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din dismissed his steward's words, recalling a poet’s verse instead.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁没理会管家的话，反而想起了诗人的一句诗句。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din declared he would not worry about his supper if he had enough for his morning meal. The steward agreed, leaving as Nur al-Din continued his lavish lifestyle. He gave away orchards, houses, and baths to anyone who asked, living a year of daily banquets.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁宣誓说，只要他早上的饭有着落，晚上吃饭他就不会操心。管家同意了他的说法，随后便离开了，而努尔·丁继续过着奢侈的生活。他把果园、房屋和浴室赠予求者，一年下来天天都在举办盛宴。

paragraphs.en: One day, while listening to Anis al-Jalis sing:
paragraphs.zh: 有一天，当安妮丝·阿吉勒斯正在唱歌时，我听到了她的歌声：

paragraphs.en: You thought well of the days when they were good, Oblivious to the ills fate brings to one. You were deluded by the peaceful nights, Yet in the peace of night does sorrow stun,
paragraphs.zh: 你曾对那些美好的日子抱有好感，却未曾料到命运会带来种种不幸。你被宁静的夜晚所迷惑，然而在夜的平静中，悲伤悄然而至。

paragraphs.en: there was a knock at the door. A guest announced, "My lord Nur al-Din, there is knocking..."
paragraphs.zh: 门敲了一下。一位客人通报说：“我的主诺尔丁大人，有人在敲门……”

paragraphs.en: But morning interrupted Shahrazad's story, and she paused. Dinarzad remarked, "What an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 但晨光打断了沙赫拉兹达的故事，她停了下来。丁纳札德remark道：“这故事真引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹达回答说：“如果国王饶恕我，那就等明晚吧。”

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that one of the guests said there was knocking at the door. Nur al-Din Ali rose to open it, followed by his companion unaware. The steward stood outside and, when asked what was wrong, replied that all of Nur al-Din's possessions were gone.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，有位客人说有人在敲门。努尔·丁·阿里站起身要去开门，他的同伴却浑然不知。管家站在门外，被问及何事时回答说，努尔·丁的所有财物都不见了。

paragraphs.en: Upon hearing this, Nur al-Din bowed his head in acceptance.
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，努尔·阿丁低下了头表示认同。

paragraphs.en: The man who secretly followed Nur al-Din returned to his companions and suggested they leave him alone now that he was bankrupt. They agreed not to stay with him. Nur al-Din dismissed the steward and then called Anis al-Jalis.
paragraphs.zh: 那个秘密跟踪努尔·阿丁的男子回到同伴身边，建议他们现在让他独自去吧，毕竟他已经破产了。同伴们同意不再跟着他。努尔·阿丁辞退了管家，然后叫来了安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯。

paragraphs.en: When she arrived, he told her of the steward's news. She reminded him that his family and friends had warned him but he ignored them.
paragraphs.zh: 她一到，他就告诉她管家带来的消息。她提醒他，家人和朋友早就警告过他，但他却置之不理。

paragraphs.en: Anis al-Jalis quoted a poem: "If fortune befriend you be kind to all, / Before she slips away and lets you down. / Munificence will not undo it if she smile, / And avarice will not preserve it if she frown." She urged Nur al-Din to reflect on his situation.
paragraphs.zh: 安伊斯·阿吉勒斯引用了一首诗：“倘若命运垂青你，请善待众人，/ 在她转瞬即逝、弃你不顾之前。/ 慷慨不会因她的微笑而消失无踪，/ 贪婪也无法在她皱眉时将其挽留。”她敦促努尔·丁思考自己的处境。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din approached his ten friends but found none at home. He knocked on the first door, and a maid replied that their master was not there. Disappointed, Nur al-Din went to the second house, only to hear the same response.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿德丁走近他的十位朋友家中，却发现无人在家。他敲了第一扇门，一个女仆回答说他们的主人不在。失望之余，努尔·阿德丁前往第二户人家，结果听到的依然是同样的答复。

paragraphs.en: Reflecting on these rejections, he recited:
paragraphs.zh: 反思这些拒绝后，他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: "When affluent, a man is like a tree, Round which people collect as long as fruit they see. But when the fruit is gone, they turn away And leave the tree to dust and misery."
paragraphs.zh: “当一个人手头宽裕时，就像一棵果树，人们围绕着他，只要还能看到果实。但一旦果实耗尽，人们便会转身离去，将树遗弃在尘土和困苦之中。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din felt his hopes fading.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁感到自己的希望渐渐消逝。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, Shahrazad paused her story. Dinarzad remarked, "What an intriguing tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more to share if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的讲述。丁尔札德remark道：“这故事真引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹 aden答道：“等明天晚上见分晓吧；如果国王饶恕我，我还会有更多精彩的故事与你分享。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din returned to Anis al-Jalis feeling more depressed than before. She asked him, "My lord, do you believe me now?" He replied, "Not one of them would take any notice of me or ask me in."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁回到安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯身边时显得更加沮丧。她问他：“我的主人，你现在相信我了吗？”他回答说：“他们中没有一个人会注意到我或邀请我。”

paragraphs.en: Anis suggested selling some furniture and utensils until God provided for them. Nur al-Din began to sell the items gradually, living on the proceeds until nothing was left.
paragraphs.zh: 安伊斯建议卖掉一些家具和器具，直到上帝为他们提供帮助。努尔·丁开始逐渐出售这些物品，靠卖东西的钱生活，直到最后一件也没剩下。

paragraphs.en: Then he turned to Anis and asked, "What is left to sell now?" She replied, "O my lord, it is my advice that you should rise at once and take me down to the market and sell me. Your father bought me for ten thousand dinars; perhaps God will help you get close to this amount."
paragraphs.zh: 然后他转向安妮斯问道：“现在还有什么可卖的？”她回答说：“我的主人，我建议您立刻起身带我去市场卖掉自己吧。父亲当初花了十万里尔才买下我；或许真主会帮助你接近这个数目。”

paragraphs.en: She added, "If it is His will to reunite us, we will meet again."
paragraphs.zh: 她又说：“如果真主愿意让我们重逢，我们终会再相见。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din replied, "O Anis al-Jalis, by God, I cannot endure to be parted from you one single hour." Anis said, "By God, my lord, nor can I; but necessity compels, as the poet says: Necessity compels us to resort Sometimes to ways that decent men oppose. No man forces himself to do a thing, except what is dictated by the cause."
paragraphs.zh: 奴仆 girl 安伊斯·阿吉勒斯回答说：“安纳尔丁，天哪，我无法忍受与你分开哪怕一个小时。”安伊斯说道：“安纳尔丁大人，我也一样；但 necessity 强迫我们有时不得不采取体面人反对的方式。没有人会强迫自己去做某事，除非出于原因的驱使。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din rose and took Anis with him, his tears running profusely over his cheeks. He said, "Stay and give me a final look before we part, so that I may console my heart, which wastes away." But if you deem this burdensome, I'd rather die of love than on you such a burden lay.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁站起身，带着安斯一同离开，泪水在他脸颊上恣意流淌。他说道：“留下来再看我一眼，让我们分别前有个交代，也好慰藉我那日渐枯萎的心灵。”但如果你觉得这样太过沉重，我还是宁愿死于相思，也不愿让你承受这份负担。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din entered the market with Anis al-Jalis and delivered her to Haj Hasan, one of the brokers. The broker replied, "O my lord Nur al-Din, your interest is protected." He added, "Isn't she Anis al-Jalis, whom your father bought some time ago for ten thousand dinars?"
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁带着安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯走进市场，并把她交给了哈吉·哈桑，一名经纪人。经纪人回答道：“我的主人努尔·阿丁，您的利益得到了保障。”他又补充说，“她不是你们父亲不久前以一万第纳尔买下的安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯吗？”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din confirmed, "Yes, she is."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁确认道：“是的，她就是。”

paragraphs.en: The broker looked around and saw that many merchants were still absent. He waited until the market began to get very active, with all kinds of girls being sold—Nubians, Europeans, Greeks, Circassians, Turks, Tartars, and others. When the market was very active, the broker rose and went up to the merchants, crying out, "O merchants..."
paragraphs.zh: 经纪人环顾四周，发现许多商人都还未到场。他等到市场变得十分热闹，各种肤色的女孩都被摆了出来——有努比亚人、欧洲人、希腊人、卡巴尔达人、土耳其人、土库曼人以及其他各色人等。当市场熙熙攘攘时，经纪人站起身来，走上前去，喊道：“各位商人……”

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached. Dinarzad then remarked to her sister, "That was a strange and engaging tale!" Shahrazad responded, "Wait until tomorrow night; there's an even stranger story coming if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 随着晨光渐近，沙赫拉兹默不作声。迪纳兹达 then 说道：“那个故事真是奇怪又引人入胜！”沙赫拉兹回答道：“等到明天晚上再说吧；如果国王饶恕我，还会有更离奇的故事等着你听呢。”

paragraphs.en: The next evening, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹朵开始说道：

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that the broker cried out, "O merchants, not every round thing a walnut nor every long thing a banana; not every red thing meat nor every white thing fat. I have here this unique pearl." One of them bid four thousand dinars, but while he was calling for bids, Vizier al-Mu'in ibn-Sawi passed by and noticed Nur al-Din standing in the corner.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，那经纪人喊道：“商人们，不是每个圆的东西都是核桃，也不是每个长的东西都是香蕉；不是每件红的东西都是肉，也不是每件白的东西都是肥膘。我这里有一颗独一无二的珍珠。”其中一个商人出价四千第纳尔，但就在他叫价的时候，穆因·本·萨瓦伊 vizier 阁下恰好经过，并注意到努尔丁站在角落里。

paragraphs.en: Al-Mu'in thought to himself, "I wonder what ibn-Khaqan is doing here. Has this good-for-nothing anything left to buy girls with?" Seeing the broker surrounded by merchants, he called him over.
paragraphs.zh: 阿穆因心想：“不知伊本-哈agan来这里做什么。这家伙还能用什么买女奴？”只见商人们围在中间，他便朝那个经纪人喊道。

paragraphs.en: The broker, who dared not cross the Vizier, showed Nur al-Din's slave-girl Anis al-Jalis. Al-Mu'in bid four thousand dinars and ordered the broker to offer the same amount to Nur al-Din. When the merchants heard this, they did not dare to bid against him.
paragraphs.zh: 那位不敢得罪 vizier 的经纪人将奴婢安妮丝·阿尔贾利斯介绍给了努尔丁。穆因开价四千第纳尔，并命令经纪人向努尔丁提出同样的报价。听到这话，商人们都不敢与之竞价。

paragraphs.en: The broker went to Nur al-Din and warned him that if he accepted the Vizier's note, it would only delay payment. Al-Mu'in would send his agents to procrastinate, promising to pay later but never doing so.
paragraphs.zh: 经纪人去找努尔·阿丁，警告他说如果接受 vizier 的欠条，只会拖延付款。穆因会派他的代理人故意拖拖拉拉，承诺日后支付却从未履行诺言。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din asked for advice. The broker suggested a clever plan: when in the middle of the market, Nur al-Din should slap Anis al-Jalis and say, "O slut, see how I have fulfilled my pledge by bringing you here to sell you at auction." Al-Mu'in would be fooled into believing that Nur al-Din brought her there only as a fulfillment of his promise.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁寻求建议。经纪人提出了一个巧妙的计划：当他们在市场中心时，努尔·丁应该掴了安妮斯一巴掌，并喊道：“贱货，看看我如何履行诺言，把你带到这儿来拍卖。”穆因会被蒙在鼓里，以为努尔·丁只是为了兑现他的承诺才把她带到这里。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din agreed with the broker's advice.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁同意了经纪人的建议。

paragraphs.en: The broker led Anis al-Jalis to Nur al-Din ibn-Khaqan and handed her over, only for him to slap her harshly.
paragraphs.zh: 经纪人把安妮斯·阿吉勒斯带到努尔丁·哈克坎面前，刚一交到他手里，他就狠狠地打了她一巴掌。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached. Dinarzad remarked, "What a strange tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have more stories in store."
paragraphs.zh: 随着晨光渐近，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳兹阿德remark道：“这可真是个奇怪的故事！”沙赫拉兹 aden答道：“等到明天晚上再说吧；我还准备了更多的故事。”

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德接着说：

paragraphs.en: O King, Nur al-Din scolded Anis al-Jalis: "You deserve this! I brought you here as promised. Go home and learn your lesson."
paragraphs.zh: 国王啊，努尔丁责备奴隶 girl 安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯说：“你咎由自取！我如约把你带到这里。你回去好好反省吧。”

paragraphs.en: He then turned to the vizier, who had intervened, and threatened him with violence.
paragraphs.zh: 他随即转向插手的首相，威胁他说要对他施以暴力。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din, a strong young man, seized the vizier, threw him into a nearby mudhole, and began beating him. The vizier's ten Mamluks were ready to intervene but were stopped by the merchants and bystanders, who warned them of potential future conflicts.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁是一位强壮的年轻人，他一把抓住首相，将其扔进附近的泥坑里，并开始痛打。首相的十名马穆鲁克武士本已准备干预，却被商人和旁观者劝阻了，这些人警告他们未来可能会因此引发冲突。

paragraphs.en: The crowd advised against any further violence, fearing mutual hatred or death for all involved if they interfered.
paragraphs.zh: 人群中有人劝阻不要进一步施暴，担心如果干预会导致彼此憎恨或所有人都陷入悲剧。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din finished beating the vizier and took Anis al-Jalis home. The vizier, covered in mud and blood, cried out to King Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman al-Zainabi, "O King of the age, I am a man aggrieved." The king summoned him and asked, "Who has done this to you?"
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁打完了 vizier，将奴隶 girl 安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯送回了家。vizier 身上沾满了泥巴和血迹，向穆罕默德·本-萨勒曼·扎伊纳比国王喊道：“哦，时代的君王，我是一个蒙冤的人。”国王召见了他，并问道：“是谁对你做了这种事？”

paragraphs.en: The vizier wept and recited:
paragraphs.zh: vizier 哭泣着吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: Shall bad fortune oppress me while you live? Shall wolves eat me while you stand, a lion strong and proud? Shall every thirsty man drink from your store, While I go thirsty, O rain-laden cloud?
paragraphs.zh: 你活着的时候，难道不幸会降临到我头上？你站着如同一头雄狮，威武不屈，而狼群却要吞噬我吗？你储藏的甘露为何让别人畅饮，而我只能望天兴叹，像一片载雨的乌云？

paragraphs.en: He then explained that he had gone to the slave market to buy a cook when he saw Anis al-Jalis. The broker informed him that she belonged to Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Khaqan. Previously, King Muhammad had given his father ten thousand dinars to purchase a girl for the king, but after she pleased the father, Nur al-Din's father gave her to him.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后解释说，自己原本是去奴隶市场买一名厨师，没想到却遇到了安妮丝·阿尔吉拉斯。中间人告诉他，这名女子属于努尔丁·阿里·本-哈卡恩。此前，穆罕默德国王曾给他的父亲一万第纳尔，让他为国王购买一名女孩，但当这女孩让父亲满意后，努尔丁的父亲便将她转给了他。

paragraphs.en: Upon his death, Nur al-Din sold everything and brought Anis al-Jalis to the market. The broker auctioned her, and merchants bid until it reached four thousand dinars. Nur al-Din then asked the vizier to buy her for the king with that money.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁去世后，他卖掉了所有财产，并将安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯带到市场上。经纪人拍卖了她，商人们你争我夺，最终出价四千第纳尔。随后，努尔·丁请 vizier 用这笔钱为国王买下了安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: O happy king, I heard that al-Mu'in ibn-Sawi said to the king, "Nur al-Din looked at me and declared, 'Wretched old man, I will sell her to a Christian or Jew rather than to you.' I retorted, 'Is this how you repay our lord for his kindness?' He then beat me until I lay injured.
paragraphs.zh: 哦，幸福的国王，我听说阿慕因·本-萨维对国王说：“努尔·丁看着我说，‘可怜的老家伙，我要把她卖给基督徒或犹太人，而不是卖给你。’ 我反驳道：‘你这样回报我们的主人的恩惠吗？’ 他随后打了我一顿，直到我受伤倒地。

paragraphs.en: This happened because I tried to be loyal to you." The vizier fell to the ground, weeping and pretending to faint.
paragraphs.zh: “这是因为我想对你忠心。”宰相扑倒在地，哭着装作昏了过去。

paragraphs.en: The king's eyes bulged with anger upon hearing this. Turning to his officers, he ordered, "Go to ibn-Khaqan’s house, sack it, and bring him and the girl here." One of the chamberlains, Alam al-Din Sanjar, who had once served Fadl al-Din but now worked for the king, could not bear seeing Nur al-Din in danger.
paragraphs.zh: 国王一听这话，怒目圆睁。他转向手下的官员们命令道：“去把伊本-哈夸恩的房子抄个干净，把他和那个女孩都带到这里来。”曾经侍奉过法尔德丁·阿丁，如今却为国王效力的殿臣阿拉姆丁·桑贾尔见 Nur al-Din 陷入危险之中，心中无法忍受。

paragraphs.en: He left the court, mounted his horse, and rode to Nur al-Din’s house.
paragraphs.zh: 他离开了宫廷，骑上马匹，径直前往努尔·丁的住所。

paragraphs.en: Knocking on the door, Nur al-Din emerged. Seeing it was Sanjar, he greeted him. But Sanjar replied, "Not now for greetings."
paragraphs.zh: 敲门声响起，努尔·阿丁走了出来。见到是桑贾尔，他上前打了声招呼。但桑贾尔回应说：“现在不是寒暄的时候。”

paragraphs.en: Quoting a poet, he said, "If you suffer injustice, save yourself / And leave the house behind to mourn its builder. / Your country you'll replace by another, / But for yourself you'll find no other self. / Nor with a mission trust another man, / For none is as loyal as you yourself."
paragraphs.zh: 引用一位诗人的诗句，他说道：“如果你蒙受不公，自救为上/ 离开那栋房子，让建造者独自哀悼。/ 你可换一个国家，却难寻另一个自我。/ 不要将重任托付他人，因为无人能如你忠诚。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis fled quickly after ‘Alam al-Din warned them of the vizier’s trap. The king had sent forty armed men to capture them. They found safety at the riverbank, where a large ship was ready to sail.
paragraphs.zh: 阿拉姆丁警告他们 vizier 设下的陷阱后，努尔丁和安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯迅速逃走。国王派了四十名武装士兵来捉拿他们。他们在河边找到了避难所，那里有一艘大船正准备启航。

paragraphs.en: Morning interrupted Shahrazad's storytelling, but Dinarzad praised her tale as strange and entertaining. Shahrazad promised an even better story if she survived another night with the king.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光打断了沙赫拉兹阿德的讲述，但丁扎兹阿德称赞她的故事新奇且引人入胜。沙赫拉兹阿德承诺，如果她能再陪国王度过一个夜晚，一定会带来更加精彩的故事。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din boarded the ship with Anis al-Jalis and asked the captain where they were heading. The captain replied that they were bound for Baghdad. As the boat sailed, it moved swiftly, as if its sails were wings, much like a bird diving into water.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁与奴隶 girl 安伊斯·阿尔-贾利斯一起登上了船只，并询问船长他们将要去往哪里。船长回答说他们会驶向巴格达。随着船只航行，它快速前行，仿佛帆布成了翅膀，如同一只鸟儿一头扎入水中。

paragraphs.en: The poet described the ship's speed and grace, comparing it to lightning and a thirsty bird swooping down to drink.
paragraphs.zh: 诗人描述了船只的速度与优雅，将其比作闪电般迅捷和口渴的鸟儿俯冲饮水。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, the Mamluks, sent by the king, searched Nur al-Din's house but found neither him nor Anis al-Jalis. After ransacking the place, they reported back to the king. The king ordered them to search everywhere and bring Nur al-Din to him if found.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，国王派来的马穆鲁克士兵搜查了努尔·丁的住所，却既未发现努尔·丁本人，也未找到奴隶 girl 安尼斯·阿尔-贾利斯。经过一番翻箱倒柜之后，他们向国王汇报了情况。国王命令他们彻底搜寻，并如果发现努尔·丁的话一定要把他带回来。

paragraphs.en: They returned with a robe of honor for the vizier and comforting words from the king, who vowed to avenge the vizier.
paragraphs.zh: 他们带着一件荣典袍返回，赠予 vizier，并带来了国王安慰的话语，表示要为 vizier 报仇。

paragraphs.en: In the meantime, Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis sailed under favorable winds. God granted them safe passage, and they arrived in Baghdad, the city of Peace. The captain congratulated Nur al-Din on their arrival, describing Baghdad as teeming with life, full of spring's beauty, and a place where streams flowed and birds sang.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，努尔·阿丁和安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯在顺风中航行。上帝赐予他们平安的旅程，使他们抵达了和平之城巴格达。船长对努尔·阿丁的到来表示祝贺，描述巴格达生机勃勃，充满春天的美丽，溪流潺潺，鸟语花香。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din gave the captain five dinars before disembarking with Anis al-Jalis. They wandered until they found an alley surrounded by gardens. The alley was well-swept and watered, with long benches and cooling pots full of cold water.
paragraphs.zh: 奴仆女孩安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯和努尔丁·阿里·本-哈卡恩的故事 努尔丁下了船，给了船长五迪纳尔，然后带着安伊斯·阿尔·贾利斯四处游荡。他们最终发现了一条被花园环绕的小巷。这条小巷打扫得干干净净，还经常浇水，两旁设有长长的木凳和装满冷水的凉亭。

paragraphs.en: A hanging trellis led to a garden gate that was shut.
paragraphs.zh: 悬挂在上方的藤架通向一扇紧闭的花园门。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din suggested resting on the bench. After drinking some water and washing their hands and faces, they sat down. As they were caressed by the breeze, they heard the sounds of birds singing, doves cooing in the trees, and the murmur of streams.
paragraphs.zh: 奴婢安妮丝·阿尔·贾利斯和努尔丁·阿里·本-哈卡恩的故事 努尔丁建议他们在长凳上休息。喝了一些水，洗了洗手脸后，他们坐了下来。微风轻拂，他们听到了鸟儿的歌唱声，树上的斑鸠咕咕叫着，还有溪流潺潺的声音。

paragraphs.en: They soon fell asleep.
paragraphs.zh: 他们很快就睡着了。

paragraphs.en: In Baghdad, Harun al-Rashid's Garden of Delight was unmatched. Inside stood the Palace of Statues, where he would retreat when depressed. The palace had eighty windows and hanging lamps flanking candelabras with large candles.
paragraphs.zh: 在巴格达，哈伦·拉什德的欢娱园无人能及。园内有一座雕像宫，他心情低落时便会退居于此。这座宫殿有八十扇窗户，烛台两侧悬挂着灯盏，上面插着大蜡烛。

paragraphs.en: Upon entering, Harun would order all windows opened, lamps lit, and his singer Ishak al-Nadim to perform while surrounded by concubines.
paragraphs.zh: 一进门，哈伦便吩咐打开所有窗户，点亮灯烛，并让歌手伊沙克·纳迪姆在众姬妾的环绕中表演。

paragraphs.en: Shaikh Ibrahim, the garden's keeper, was a man of great affection to the caliph. However, whenever Shaikh Ibrahim left for business in the city, he found pleasure-seekers and their prostitutes gathered at the garden gate, which saddened him. One day, Harun al-Rashid noticed this and intervened.
paragraphs.zh: 沙基克·易布拉欣是花园的管理员，对哈里发极为体贴。然而每当他进城处理事务时，总能看到一些寻欢作乐的人和妓女聚集在花园门口，这让他感到十分沮丧。一天，哈伦·拉什德注意到了这个问题并出面干预了。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad paused her story. Dinarzad then said, "What a fascinating tale!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have an even more captivating story to share if the king spares me."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的讲述。迪纳兹达then说道：“这故事真精彩！”沙赫拉兹adeon答道：“等到明天夜晚再听吧；如果国王饶恕我，我还有一段更加引人入胜的故事要与你分享。”

paragraphs.en: Ibrahim, the gardener, waited for the caliph's permission to deal with anyone found at the gate. On Nur al-Din’s arrival day, Ibrahim returned from a city errand to find two people sleeping under a cloak near the entrance. He considered beating them but decided to uncover their faces first.
paragraphs.zh: 园丁易卜拉欣在等待哈里发批准处理任何出现在门口的人。努尔·阿丁抵达的那天，易卜拉欣从城里办完事回来，发现有两个陌生人蜷缩在一顶斗篷下熟睡。他本打算教训他们一顿，但还是决定先掀开斗篷看看他们的脸。

paragraphs.en: Seeing their radiant beauty, he covered them again and approached Nur al-Din.
paragraphs.zh: 见到她们光彩照人的容颜，他不禁又将她们遮掩起来，然后走近努尔丁。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din woke up, feeling embarrassed when an old man began rubbing his feet. He drew back, sat up, and kissed the hand of the old man, calling him uncle. Ibrahim asked where they came from, and Nur al-Din replied that they were strangers.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿德丁醒来时，感到有些尴尬，因为一位老人开始给他按摩脚。他往后一缩，坐了起来，并向那位老人吻手，称呼他为叔叔。伊布拉欣问他们是从哪里来的，努尔·阿德丁回答说他们是陌生人。

paragraphs.en: The old man invited them into the garden to relax, assuring them it was his inheritance.
paragraphs.zh: 老者邀请他们进入花园休息，保证说这是他的遗产。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din thanked Ibrahim and followed him with Anis al-Jalis into the garden.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁感谢了伊布拉欣，随后与奴隶 girl 安伊斯·阿勒·吉拉斯一同走进花园。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din and Dinarzad entered a garden through an arched gateway that reminded them of Paradise. The bower was adorned with trellised branches covered in grapes of various colors—red like rubies, black like Abyssinian faces, and white like pearls. Inside the garden, they saw birds singing sweetly: nightingales, pigeons, thrushes, larks, and turtledoves.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁和迪纳兹德穿过一座拱门进入了花园，那扇门让他们想起了天堂。园中的凉亭装饰着攀爬的枝条，上面挂满了各种颜色的葡萄——红如红宝石，黑似埃塞俄比亚人的脸庞，白若珍珠。走进花园，他们听见鸟儿们婉转地歌唱：夜莺、鸽子、画眉、云雀和斑鸠。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. Dinarzad said, "What a fascinating story!" Shahrazad replied, "Wait until tomorrow night; I have an even better one for you."
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹默不作声。丁纳扎德说道：“真是个引人入胜的故事！”沙赫拉兹回应道：“你得等到明天晚上了；我还有个更好听的给你。”

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began her tale: When Nur al-Din saw the beautiful garden, it brought back memories of his happy times with friends. He turned to the old man and asked, "What is your name?" The old man replied, "I am Ibrahim."
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德开始了她的讲述：当努尔·丁看到那片美丽的花园时，不禁想起了与朋友们快乐相处的时光。他转头对那位老人问道：“您尊姓大名？”老人回答说：“我叫易卜拉欣。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din said, "Shaikh Ibrahim, this garden is wonderful. May God bless you with it. Shaikh Ibrahim, we appreciate your hospitality but only need two dinars for some bread and meat."
paragraphs.zh: 奴尔·阿丁说道：“伊布拉欣老师，这个花园真是美不胜收。愿真主赐福于你。伊布拉欣老师，我们感谢你的款待，但只求给你两第纳尔买些面包和肉。”

paragraphs.en: Ibrahim gladly accepted the money, thinking they would eat little and keep the rest. He left to buy them plenty of good food.
paragraphs.zh: 易卜拉欣高兴地收下了钱，心想他们可以少吃一些，把剩下的留着。随后他出去买了许多好吃的东西。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis wandered through the garden until they reached the Palace of Statues. Despite its grandeur, they were unable to enter. Upon returning from the market, Shaikh Ibrahim was asked by Nur al-Din about ownership of the palace.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁和安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯在花园中漫步，直到来到了雕像宫。尽管这座宫殿气势宏伟，但他们却无法进入。努尔·阿丁从市场上回来后，被问及雕像宫的所有权问题时，伊布拉欣长老向他提出了这个问题。

paragraphs.en: When Shaikh Ibrahim hesitated, he eventually admitted that it belonged to him as well. Feeling embarrassed and obligated, Shaikh Ibrahim returned with a key, opened the door, and invited them inside.
paragraphs.zh: 当伊布拉欣 Sheikh Ibrahim 犹豫不决时，最终承认这把钥匙也属于他。感到有些尴尬和不得不这么做，伊布拉欣带着一把钥匙回来了，打开了门，请他们进去。

paragraphs.en: Inside, they walked through the palace until reaching an elevated hall. As Nur al-Din admired the windows, hanging lamps, and candelabras, he exclaimed, "By God, this is a beautiful place!"
paragraphs.zh: Inside，他们穿过宫殿，直到来到一个高大的厅堂。努尔·阿丁欣赏着窗户、悬挂的灯饰和烛台，不禁脱口而出：“真主作证，这里真是个美丽的地方！”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis finished their meal and washed their hands. Nur al-Din then went to a window, opened it, and called out to Anis al-Jalis, who joined him to admire the fruit-laden trees outside.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁和安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯吃完饭后洗了洗手。随后，努尔·丁走到窗前，推开窗户，朝外喊道，安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯也走了过来，两人一起欣赏着窗外果实累累的树木。

paragraphs.en: Afterward, Nur al-Din turned to the old man and asked, "Shaikh, do you have anything to drink?" The old man replied that they usually drank before eating. Nur al-Din explained that people often drink after their meal.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，努尔·阿丁转向那位老人问道：“谢赫，您有饮料吗？”老人回答说他们通常是在进食之前喝的。努尔·阿丁解释道，人们常常是在饭后才喝水解渴。

paragraphs.en: The old man was surprised, exclaiming, "You don’t mean wine?"
paragraphs.zh: 老人惊讶地喊道：“你不会是说酒吧？”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din confirmed it. The old man, shocked, said he had made the Holy Pilgrimage thirteen times and never mentioned such a word. Nur al-Din proposed a test: if an ass tied in the corner was cursed, would the curse fall on the old man?
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁确认了这一点。老人震惊不已，表示自己已经完成了十三次朝圣之旅，从未说过这样的话。努尔·丁提议进行一个测试：如果角落里的驴子被诅咒了，那诅咒会不会降临到这位老人身上？

paragraphs.en: The old man replied no.
paragraphs.zh: 老人摇了摇头。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din then suggested the old man take two dinars and dirhams to buy wine from a wineshop. He instructed the old man to stand at a distance, call a customer, offer him money for himself, and buy two flagons of wine with the rest. After buying the wine, the old man should place it in a saddlebag on the ass and drive it back.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁随后建议那位老人拿上两枚第纳尔和迪拉姆去酒馆买些酒。他吩咐老人站在远处，招揽一位顾客，自己出钱请客，并用剩下的钱买两壶酒。买完酒后，老人应将酒放在驴鞍囊中，然后赶着驴回去。

paragraphs.en: The old man agreed, finding Nur al-Din's suggestion amusing. He followed these instructions, returned with the wine, and Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis unloaded it.
paragraphs.zh: 老人同意了，觉得努尔·丁的建议挺有趣。他照着这些指示去做，回来时带来了酒，然后努尔·丁和安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯一起卸下了酒桶。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din then asked the old man to bring them what they needed from his storerooms, including a wine service and utensils. The old man handed over the keys and went to fetch some fruits.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁随后请那位老人从他的仓库里取来他们所需的物品，包括酒具和餐具。老人递过钥匙，转身去拿些水果。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, interrupting Shahrazad's storytelling. Dinarzad commented on how interesting the story was. Shahrazad replied that it paled in comparison to what she would tell the next night if the king spared her life.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光熹微，打断了沙赫拉兹的讲述。丁纳札德对这个故事赞不绝口。沙赫拉兹回应说，如果国王能饶她一命，她第二天晚上要讲的故事将会更加精彩。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad began:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，舍赫拉查德开口说道：

paragraphs.en: O happy king, Shaikh Ibrahim said, "Take what you need." Nur al-Din opened all storerooms and cupboards, while the old man brought fruits and flowers. Anis al-Jalis prepared the table with cups, beakers, gold and silver utensils, nuts, and fruits.
paragraphs.zh: 贤明的君王，沙希克伊布拉欣说道：“拿你需要的东西。”努尔丁打开了所有的仓库和橱柜，而那位老人则端来了水果和鲜花。安伊斯阿勒吉拉斯准备好了餐桌，摆上了杯子、小壶、金器银器餐具、坚果和水果。

paragraphs.en: They sat to drink when Nur al-Din filled a cup and said to Anis al-Jalis:
paragraphs.zh: 他们坐下来喝酒，这时努尔·阿丁给安伊斯·阿尔-贾利斯倒了一杯，说道：

paragraphs.en: "Our journey has proved most fortunate by coming to this garden."
paragraphs.zh: “我们的旅程因来到这个花园而变得格外幸运。”

paragraphs.en: He recited:
paragraphs.zh: 他吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: O what a lovely and perfect day, What charm, what joy, and total bliss! My right hand holds the cup, my left the moon; Why heed the one who censures me for this?
paragraphs.zh: 啊，多么美好而完美的日子！怎样的魅力，怎样的欢乐，以及无上的幸福！我的右手持杯，左手揽月；为何要在意那些对我如此行为指手画脚的人呢？

paragraphs.en: They drank until night fell. Shaikh Ibrahim returned to check if they needed anything else. Standing at the door, he said to Nur al-Din:
paragraphs.zh: 他们喝到夜幕降临。伊布拉欣长老回来查看是否还需要什么。他站在门口对努尔·丁说道：

paragraphs.en: "My lord, by God, this is a happy day, For you have honored me with your presence."
paragraphs.zh: 我的主人，真主作证，今天真是喜庆的日子，您光临使我倍感荣幸。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din, now drunk, replied:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁现在醉了，脱口而出：“你说得对。”

paragraphs.en: "O Shaikh Ibrahim, far be it from you to be honored by us. By God, we have imposed on your goodness and fully enjoyed your generosity."
paragraphs.zh: “伊布拉欣阿訇，这可使不得。真主作证，我们这是冒昧接受了您的好意，享受了您的慷慨。”

paragraphs.en: Anis al-Jalis turned to her lord, Nur al-Din, and suggested, "My lord, what if we make Shaikh Ibrahim drink?" Nur al-Din asked, "Can you do that?" She replied confidently, "Yes."
paragraphs.zh: 安伊斯·阿尔吉拉斯转向她的主人努尔丁，建议道：“我的主，我们让伊布拉欣谢赫喝一点如何？”努尔丁问道：“你能做到吗？”她自信地回答：“当然可以。”

paragraphs.en: He then invited the old man, who reluctantly joined them. As they drank, their faces flushed, foreheads perspired, and eyes sparkled. Nur al-Din urged Shaikh Ibrahim to sit with them, but the old man eventually complied.
paragraphs.zh: 他随后邀请了那位老人，老人勉强加入了他们。随着饮酒的进行，他们的脸庞渐渐泛红，额头渗出汗珠，眼睛闪烁着光芒。努尔·丁敦促伊布拉欣长老一同坐下，最终老人还是屈从了。

paragraphs.en: Anis al-Jalis observed her lord's behavior and said, "Look how he treats me!" Nur al-Din responded, "He always drinks a little and falls asleep." Anis al-Jalis filled a cup for the old man, saying, "Be kind to me and drink."
paragraphs.zh: 安尼斯·阿尔吉拉斯观察到主人的行为，说道：“你看他怎么对待我！”努尔·丁回答道：“他总是喝点酒就睡着了。”安尼斯·阿尔吉拉斯给老人倒了一杯酒，说：“对我好一点，你也喝一杯吧。”

paragraphs.en: He drank it, but she continued, offering more. As morning approached, Shahrazad paused her story.
paragraphs.zh: 他喝完了，但她并未停止，继续递上更多的酒。随着晨光渐近，沙赫拉兹暂停了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din noticed the girl fill the fourth cup for an old man, who hesitated before drinking it. Nur al-Din questioned him, revealing his earlier refusal due to a vow of abstinence. The old man admitted he had no control over himself.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁注意到那个女孩为一位老人倒了第四杯酒，而老人在喝之前犹豫了一下。努尔·阿丁询问起这件事，揭露了老人早前因誓言禁欲而拒绝喝酒的原因。老人承认自己无法控制自己的行为。

paragraphs.en: They laughed and continued their revelry.
paragraphs.zh: 他们笑着继续狂欢。

paragraphs.en: The girl then whispered to Nur al-Din, instructing him to drink without urging the old man. As they drank together, the old man asked why he was left out. This led to more laughter and drinking until late into the night.
paragraphs.zh: 女孩随后悄悄对努尔·阿丁说，让他先喝不要催促那位老人。两人边喝边聊，老人问起自己为何被冷落。这引得他们一阵 more laughter 和继续畅饮，直到深夜。

paragraphs.en: Halfway through the night, the girl suggested lighting a candle. The old man instructed her to light only one but she lit them all, illuminating the entire palace. Nur al-Din then requested permission to light a lamp himself, following the same rule, but he too lit all the lamps, causing the palace to glow brightly.
paragraphs.zh: 夜半时分，女孩建议点燃一支蜡烛。老人让她只点一支，但她却把所有的都点亮了，整个宫殿都被照亮了。随后， Nur al-Din 要求自己也按照同样的规矩点灯，但同样地，他也把所有灯都点亮了，使得宫殿灯火通明。

paragraphs.en: The intoxicated old man declared they were more playful than him and proceeded to open all eighty windows, letting in the night air.
paragraphs.zh: 这位醉醺醺的老头宣称她们比他还顽皮，随后打开了所有的八十扇窗户，让夜风飘了进来。

paragraphs.en: The caliph, seated by a palace window overlooking the Tigris River, saw the Palace of Statues aglow. Enraged, he called for Vizier Ja’far and demanded to know why Baghdad was lit if it had not been taken from him.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发坐在宫殿窗口旁，俯瞰着底格里斯河，只见雕像宫灯火通明。他怒不可遏，叫来首相贾法尔，质问为何巴格达会灯火通明，难道没有被夺走吗？

paragraphs.en: Ja’far trembled as he replied, "O Commander of the Faithful, these are harsh words." The caliph retorted, "If Baghdad is safe, why would anyone light the palace? Only I could authorize such a thing."
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔颤抖着回答：“哦，哈里发陛下，这些话太过严厉了。”哈里发反驳道：“如果巴格达平安无事，为什么有人会点燃宫殿？这样的事情只有我才有权批准。”

paragraphs.en: Ja’far explained that Shaikh Ibrahim had come to him last Friday, requesting permission for his sons' circumcision. He claimed he had forgotten to inform the caliph and suggested Ibrahim only wanted permission, not money.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔解释说，伊布拉欣谢赫上周五来找他，请求为他的儿子进行割礼。他声称自己忘记了通知哈里发，并建议伊布拉欣只是需要许可，并不需要支付费用。

paragraphs.en: The caliph accused Ja’far of two offenses: failing to report the request and misunderstanding its true nature as a plea for financial assistance. Ja’far admitted he was distracted.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发指控贾法尔犯了两项罪过：没有上报请求，以及误解了其真实性质——这是一个求援的请求。贾法尔承认自己分心了。

paragraphs.en: The caliph vowed to stay with Ja’far all night, believing their mutual presence would benefit both—Ja’far by his approval, and him by meeting pious men.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发发誓整晚都要留在贾法尔身边，他认为双方共处一室对彼此都有好处——对贾法尔来说是得到了他的认可，而对他来说则是结识了一些虔诚的人。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默然不语。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad said:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙赫拉兹德说道：

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad told the king that the caliph planned to visit a gathering of pious men. Ja’far was uncertain but obeyed. The caliph, along with Ja’far and Masrur, disguised as merchants, left the palace and walked through Baghdad until they reached a garden.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德对国王说，哈里发打算访问一群虔诚信徒。贾法尔虽然有些犹豫，但还是遵命行事。哈里发、贾法尔和马斯鲁尔乔装打扮成商人，离开了王宫，在巴格达街头漫步，最终来到了一个花园。

paragraphs.en: The caliph approached the open gate, surprised by its unusual state. He suggested Shaikh Ibrahim had been distracted by festivities. They entered the garden and made their way to the palace.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发走近那扇敞开的门，对它的异常状态感到惊讶。他推测艾布·伊布拉欣 Sheikh Ibrahim 被庆典分散了注意力。两人走进花园，径直朝宫殿走去。

paragraphs.en: The caliph wanted to observe secretly before joining them.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发想悄悄观察一阵再加入他们。

paragraphs.en: He spotted a tall tree near the windows and climbed it. From his vantage point, he saw a young man and woman who appeared radiant like moons. Shaikh Ibrahim held a wine cup and said:
paragraphs.zh: 他注意到窗边有一棵高大的树，便爬了上去。从这有利的位置上，他看到一对年轻男女，宛如明月般光彩照人。伊布拉欣谢赫端着酒杯说道：

paragraphs.en: "Wine without song is better left in the jug; even horses need whistling to drink."
paragraphs.zh: 酒无歌伴宁放在壶中；就连马也需要呼唤才能饮水。

paragraphs.en: When the caliph saw Shaikh Ibrahim drinking with Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis, his eyes bulged in anger. He ordered Ja’far to climb the tree for a better view. Upon seeing this, Ja’far turned pale and feared he was in trouble.
paragraphs.zh: 当哈里发看到伊布拉欣 Sheikh Ibrahim 和努尔·丁 Nur al-Din 以及安伊斯·阿尔-贾利斯 Anis al-Jalis 在一起饮酒时，他的眼睛怒目圆睁。他命令贾法尔 Ja’far 爬上树去获得更好的视角。见此情景，贾法尔面色苍白，害怕自己惹上了麻烦。

paragraphs.en: Descending from the tree, Ja’far stood before the caliph, who remarked that they had arrived just in time for the circumcision ceremony. However, Ja’far was too embarrassed to respond. The caliph then asked who allowed these guests into his palace and expressed admiration for their beauty.
paragraphs.zh: 从树上下来，贾法尔站在哈里发面前。哈里发remarked说他们正好赶上了割礼仪式。然而，贾法尔感到尴尬，没有回应。接着，哈里发问是谁允许这些客人进入他的宫殿，并称赞他们的美貌。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far tried to appease him by agreeing with the caliph's assessment. The caliph suggested climbing a branch opposite the window to watch them. Ascending together, they heard Shaikh Ibrahim ask Anis al-Jalis what was needed to complete their feast.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔试图安抚他，同意哈里发的评价。哈里发建议他们爬到窗户对面的一根树枝上，以便观看。两人一起攀上枝头，听到伊布拉欣 Sheikh 询问安妮斯·阿尔-吉拉斯需要什么才能完成他们的盛宴。

paragraphs.en: Anis replied that if they had a musical instrument, their joy would be perfect.
paragraphs.zh: 安伊斯回答说，如果他们有一件乐器，他们的喜悦将会更加完美。

paragraphs.en: That night, Shahrazad fell silent as morning approached.
paragraphs.zh: 那天晚上，随着黎明临近，莎赫拉兹德渐渐沉默了下来。

paragraphs.en: The old man produced a lute, which the caliph recognized as Ishak al-Nadim's. He declared that if Anis al-Jalis sang well, he would pardon her but hang Ja'far; otherwise, they would all face execution. Ja'far wished for poor singing to avoid hanging together.
paragraphs.zh: 老人拿出一把鲁特琴，哈里发认出这是伊沙克·纳迪姆的。他宣布如果安伊斯·阿勒吉利斯唱得好，他会宽恕她但处死贾法尔；否则，他们都将面临死刑。贾法尔希望歌声不佳以避免一同被绞死。

paragraphs.en: Anis al-Jalis began playing a melancholic tune, filling everyone with longing and sorrow. She then sang:
paragraphs.zh: 安伊斯·阿尔吉利斯开始弹奏一首忧郁的曲子，让大家充满了思念和悲伤。随后她唱道：

paragraphs.en: In love's despair, you reject us, Our pain is deserved by us. To you we appeal, for you, Listening to all who complain. Do not torment us, pitied ones, Fear the Almighty, restrain yourself.
paragraphs.zh: 在爱情的绝望中，你们拒绝了我们，我们的痛苦咎由自取。向你们求救，倾听所有诉苦之人。不要折磨我们这些可怜的人，敬畏至高无上的主，克制自己。

paragraphs.en: We fear no glory in our death, But fear being wronged again.
paragraphs.zh: 我们不畏惧死亡的荣耀，只怕再次遭受不公。

paragraphs.en: The caliph praised Anis al-Jalis's singing as the most beautiful he had ever heard. Realizing his anger was gone, Ja'far agreed. They descended from the tree, and the caliph decided to join them, hoping not to be recognized by Shaikh Ibrahim.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发称赞安伊斯·阿尔贾利斯的歌声是他听过的最美妙的。见他怒气消了，贾法尔也表示赞同。他们从树上下来，哈里发决定加入他们，希望能不被伊布拉欣谢赫认出来。

paragraphs.en: The caliph overheard fishermen below his palace one night. He had forbidden them from fishing due to a previous disturbance, but a fisherman named Karim took advantage of an open gate to catch fish undisturbed.
paragraphs.zh: 一天晚上，哈里发在宫殿中无意间听到了下面鱼市上的喧嚣声。他曾下令禁止捕鱼，因为之前发生过一起扰民事件，但一个名叫卡里姆的渔民利用宫门敞开的机会，偷偷地捕起了鱼。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent. The next night, she resumed her tale:
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹阿德默然不语。到了下一个夜晚，她重新开始了她的讲述：

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad recounted that the fisherman, upon seeing the caliph, trembled with fear and explained his actions were driven by poverty. The caliph instructed him to cast a net, which yielded various kinds of fish. Impressed, the caliph asked the fisherman to remove his patched robe and turban, then donned them himself.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德讲述说，渔夫见到哈里发后浑身颤抖，解释说自己这么做是出于贫困。哈里发命令他撒网捕鱼，结果捕获了各种各样的鱼。哈里发作色一惊，让渔夫脱下破旧的外衣和头巾，然后自己穿戴起来。

paragraphs.en: The caliph veiled his face and sent the fisherman away. He returned to the palace, placed the fish in a clean basket lined with green leaves, and knocked on Ja’far’s door. Pretending to be Karim, he claimed to have brought fish for guests.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发蒙住了脸，打发走了渔夫。他返回宫殿，将鱼放在一个铺着绿叶的干净篮子里，然后敲了敲贾法尔的门。他假装是卡里姆，声称带来了鱼招待客人。

paragraphs.en: Ja’far recognized the caliph's voice but let him enter. The caliph then went to the palace door and pretended to be Karim, asking permission to bring fish to his host.
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔认出了哈里发的声音，但仍让他进了门。随后，哈里发走到宫殿门口，假装自己是卡里姆，请求允许带鱼来拜访主人。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis were pleased when the old man mentioned fish. Anis asked him to bring them some, saying, "Please open the door for the caliph to fetch us the fish." The old man complied, and upon entering, the caliph saluted Shaikh Ibrahim, who greeted him harshly: "Welcome, you gambling thief!
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁和安伊斯·阿尔贾利斯听到提到鱼时非常高兴。安伊斯请求老者让他们弄些来，说：“请替我们去宫廷取几条鱼吧。”老者答应了，随后进入宫廷。哈里发进门后向伊布拉欣谢赫行礼，但后者冷冰冰地回应道：“欢迎你这个赌博贼！”

paragraphs.en: Show us what you have."
paragraphs.zh: “把你们的成果展示给我们。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph presented the fish. Anis commented, "By God, these are fine fish, but they would have been better if fried." Shaikh Ibrahim ordered, "Fry them yourself and bring them back," yelling at the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发端上鱼，安伊斯评论道：“真主作证，这些鱼不错，不过炸着吃会更好。”伊布拉欣谢赫命令道：“你自己给它们炸了再拿来，”对着哈里发大声喊道。

paragraphs.en: The caliph ran to Ja’far and said, "O Ja’far!" Ja’far asked, "What is the good news, O Commander of the Faithful?" The caliph replied, "They want the fish fried."
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发跑向贾法尔喊道：“贾法尔！”贾法尔问道：“陛下，有什么喜讯？”哈里发回答说：“他们要把鱼煎了。”

paragraphs.en: Ja’far offered to fry them but the caliph insisted, "By the tombs of my fathers and forefathers, none shall fry them but I."
paragraphs.zh: 贾法尔主动提出来炸制这些食物，但哈里发坚持道：“以我先祖和列祖的坟墓起誓，炸制它们的只能是我。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph returned to the keeper’s hut, where he found everything needed. He set up a stove, heated sesame oil, and fried the fish. Then he added lemons and radishes before carrying the dish back to the palace.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发回到看守的小屋，发现所需的一切都已经准备好了。他支起炉子，加热了芝麻油，煎炸了鱼肉。随后他又加入了柠檬和萝卜，将这道菜端回了宫殿。

paragraphs.en: They all ate, and Nur al-Din praised the caliph: "O fisherman, you have done us a good deed." The caliph then produced a paper purse from his pocket.
paragraphs.zh: 他们吃完后，努尔·阿丁称赞哈里发：“渔夫啊，你为我们做了件好事。”随后，哈里发从口袋里掏出一个纸制的钱袋。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Sbahrazad fell silent.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光渐亮，赛巴赫拉兹黛默不作声。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din produced a purse with thirty dinars, the remainder from his chamberlain's gift before he fled. He offered it to the caliph, saying, "O fisherman, forgive me; this is all I have. If I had known you earlier, I would have spared you poverty."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿丁掏出一个装有三十第纳尔的皮囊，这些钱是他逃走前侍从长赠予他的余款。他将皮囊递给哈里发，说道：“渔夫啊，请原谅我；这是我全部的积蓄。如果早些认识您，我本可以避免让您陷入贫困。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph, eager for music, asked Nur al-Din to let Anis al-Jalis sing.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发急切地想要听音乐，便请努尔·丁让安尼斯·阿尔·贾利斯唱歌。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din instructed Anis al-Jalis to play and sing. She tuned her lute and began:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁吩咐安伊斯·阿勒吉利斯弹奏并歌唱。她调好琴弦，开始吟唱：

paragraphs.en: The fingers of the fair caressed the strings, Ravishing the soul with her dulcet lute. And with her singing, she cured even the deaf. "Bravo!"
paragraphs.zh: 那少女白皙的手指轻抚琴弦，她的甜美的琴声令人心醉。她一开口唱歌，连聋子都能听见。“妙极了！”

paragraphs.en: cried one who had been mute.
paragraphs.zh: 一个原本沉默不语的人喊道。

paragraphs.en: She then played another measure, stunning them all, and sang:
paragraphs.zh: 她随后又弹奏了一段曲子，令所有人都为之震撼，然后唱道：

paragraphs.en: When you honored our land with your visit, You filled the air with incense, dispelling gloom. Therefore, with camphor, rosewater, and musk, My house should be perfumed.
paragraphs.zh: 您光临敝地之时，香气弥漫，驱散了阴霾。因此，我家也应该用薄荷、玫瑰水和麝香来熏香。

paragraphs.en: The caliph was delighted. Nur al-Din offered Anis al-Jalis as a gift to him. As he prepared to leave, Anis al-Jalis turned to him, saying, "Where are you going?
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发非常高兴。努尔·丁将安妮丝·阿吉勒斯作为礼物送给了他。正当他准备离开时，安妮丝·阿吉勒斯转过身来问道：“你要去哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: If you must depart, stay and hear my heart's plea."
paragraphs.zh: 如果你一定要离开，请留下听听我的心声。

paragraphs.en: She recited:
paragraphs.zh: 她吟诵道：

paragraphs.en: My memories and longing have tormented me, Until they turned me into a poor ghost. O my darling, I have not forgot you; Am still the same, still to my torments host.
paragraphs.zh: 我的思念与渴望折磨着我， 直到把我变成了一个可怜的幽灵。 哦，我的心上人，我从未忘记你； 依然是那个我，仍旧是折磨的主人。

paragraphs.en: If one could swim in his tears, I would be first. O you whose love has filled my brimming heart As wine fills up the cup to the brim, Whose love has wracked my body and soul.
paragraphs.zh: 如果我能畅游在他的泪水里，我一定第一个跳下去。哦，你那爱情填满了我这颗溢满的心，如同美酒装满了酒杯；你那爱情已将我的身心折磨得不堪重负。

paragraphs.en: The fate I dreaded has forced us apart. O Khaqan’s son, O my sole wish and hope, Who will always reign in my heart.
paragraphs.zh: 我所惧怕的命运将我们拆散。啊，哈克丹的儿子，我的唯一心愿与希望，你永远占据着我的心房。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began her tale. When the caliph heard Nur al-Din's verses, he turned to him and asked, "My lord, why did you transgress against your master? Who has a claim on you?"
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹阿德开始了她的讲述。当哈里发听到努尔·丁的诗句时，他转过身对努尔·丁说道：“我的主人啊，你为何违背了你的主人？谁对你有要求呢？”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din replied, "Fisherman, my story is extraordinary." The caliph insisted, "Tell me in prose."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁回答说：“渔夫，我的故事非常不平凡。”哈里发坚持道：“用散文告诉我吧。”

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din bowed and recited:
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁行了一礼，然后诵读道：

paragraphs.en: O my dear friend, I can no longer sleep, And my grief has increased since I left home. I had a father who loved me well, But he died under a dome, leaving me alone. Misfortunes followed, breaking my heart.
paragraphs.zh: 我亲爱的朋友，我现在再也无法入睡， 自从离家之后，我的忧伤愈发沉重。 我曾有一个疼爱我的父亲， 但他死于穹顶之下，留下我孤身一人。 不幸接踵而至，彻底粉碎了我的心。

paragraphs.en: He bought me a girl so beautiful That her fair figure put to shame the bough. I spent all on her and friends alike, Until I was forced to sell her at auction.
paragraphs.zh: 他买了一个如此美丽的女孩，她的身姿之美连树枝都自愧弗如。我把所有的钱都花在了她和朋友们身上，直到最后不得不将她拍卖出去。

paragraphs.en: When an old man bid for her, enraged, I wrested her away in anger's heat. The man struck back, but I fought him down, Knocking him out until my heart found peace.
paragraphs.zh: 当一个老人出价买她时，我愤怒不已，一把夺过她。那人反击，但我怒火中烧地与他搏斗，直到将他击倒在地，我的心中才感到平静。

paragraphs.en: Then we fled to Baghdad, where we hid From foes who envied our good fortune. You came unexpectedly and caught me short, But I gave you all I had, from hope and love.
paragraphs.zh: 然后我们逃到了巴格达，躲开了那些嫉妒我们好运的敌人。你突然出现，让我措手不及，但我还是把所有希望和爱情都给了你。

paragraphs.en: The caliph, disguised as a fisherman, promised to write a letter to King Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman, ensuring Nur al-Din's safety. However, Shahrazad fell silent at dawn.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发乔装成渔夫，承诺会写信给穆罕默德·本·苏莱曼国王，确保努尔·丁的安全。然而，沙赫拉兹尔在黎明时分沉默了。

paragraphs.en: On the following night, Shahrazad continued her tale:
paragraphs.zh: 在接下来的那个晚上，舍赫拉查德继续讲述她的故事：

paragraphs.en: O happy king, the caliph, in his guise as a fisherman, declared he would send a letter to the king, vowing no further harm. Curious, Nur al-Din questioned if a fisherman could correspond with royalty. The caliph explained they had studied together; though he was once superior, fate reversed their fortunes.
paragraphs.zh: 哦，幸福的国王哈里发，在他渔夫的身份下宣称将给另一位国王写信，并保证不会再有任何危害。好奇的 Nur al-Din 问道，一个渔夫能否与王室通信。哈里发作了解释说他们曾一起学习过；虽然他曾占上风，但命运却逆转了他们的境遇。

paragraphs.en: Yet, whenever he wrote for favors, his requests were granted.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，每当他为求恩惠而写作时，他的请求总是如愿以偿。

paragraphs.en: Hearing this, Nur al-Din agreed to let the caliph write. The caliph then penned:
paragraphs.zh: 听到这话，努尔·阿丁同意让哈里发书写。于是，哈里发作笔写下了：

paragraphs.en: From Harun al-Rashid son of al-Mahdi to His Highness Muhammad ibn-Sulaiman al-Zainabi, my cousin and heir. This letter is from Nur al-Din Ali ibn-Khaqan, vizier. Abdicate immediately; let him take your place.
paragraphs.zh: 从哈伦·拉希德，阿布杜·马赫迪之子，到尊贵的穆罕默德·本-萨利曼·扎伊纳比殿下，我的堂弟兼继承人。这封信来自宰相努尔丁·阿里·本-卡汗：立即辞职，让他接替你的位置。

paragraphs.en: Your compliance will ensure peace.
paragraphs.zh: 你的配合将会带来和平。

paragraphs.en: After sealing the letter, the caliph handed it to Nur al-Din, who kissed it reverently before placing it in his turban and departing.
paragraphs.zh: 封好信件后，哈里发把它交给了努尔·丁。努尔·丁虔诚地亲吻了信封，然后将其放入头巾中，随后离开了。

paragraphs.en: When Nur al-Din left, Ibrahim the keeper addressed the caliph: "Enough! You've brought us fish worth no more than twenty fils but received a full purse. Now you want the girl too."
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁走后，看门人伊布拉欣对哈里发说道：“够了！你给我们带来的鱼值不了二十分银币，却得到了满满一袋钱。现在你还想把女孩也据为己有。”

paragraphs.en: Earlier, when the caliph had gone to fry the fish and return, he instructed Ja’far to bring back one of his royal robes with Masrur and four armed officers, waiting below the window. The caliph would cry "Help!" if needed, then be dressed in the robe and attended by the officers.
paragraphs.zh: 先前，哈里发去煎鱼回来时，吩咐贾法尔与马苏尔及四名武装卫士在窗下等候。如果哈里发作难，可以喊“救命”，然后换上龙袍，并由卫士们陪同。

paragraphs.en: The old man spoke to the caliph: "Caliph, I'll take half the purse but no more than half of the girl." He demanded to see the contents of the purse. If it was silver, he wanted a dirham for himself; if gold, all of it.
paragraphs.zh: 老人对哈里发说：“陛下，我只要一半的钱袋，但不超过这个女孩的一半。”他要求查看钱袋的内容。如果里面是银币，他要一枚第纳尔；如果是金币，他就要全部。

paragraphs.en: For the fish, he would give a dirham's worth in change.
paragraphs.zh: 他给鱼钱的时候，只给了一个第纳尔的零头。

paragraphs.en: The caliph refused. The old man threw a porcelain plate at him, which shattered against the wall. He then went to fetch a stick from a storeroom.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发拒绝了。老人,"); 他扔出一个瓷盘，瓷盘撞在墙上摔得粉碎。随后，他走进储藏室取来一根棍子。

paragraphs.en: Morning interrupted Shahrazad as she fell silent.
paragraphs.zh: 晨曦初现时，沙赫拉兹德突然沉默了下来。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard that when the old man rushed with his stick toward the fisherman (the caliph), who was crying "Help!" from the window, he found the caliph seated and Ja’far attending. The old man was stunned, biting his nails in bewilderment.
paragraphs.zh: 我听到，当那位老人手持拐杖冲向正从窗口呼救“救命！”的渔夫（哈里发），发现哈里发已经坐在那里，贾法尔在一旁侍立时，他愣住了，不禁咬起了指甲。

paragraphs.en: He exclaimed, "Am I asleep or awake?" The caliph turned to him: "O Shaikh Ibrahim, what state do you see me in?"
paragraphs.zh: 他脱口而出：“我是在做梦吗？”哈里发转过身来对他说：“伊布拉欣老师，你看我现在是什么状态？”

paragraphs.en: The old man quickly recited a poem, becoming sober at once.
paragraphs.zh: 老者迅速吟诵了一首诗，顿时神情庄重起来。

paragraphs.en: The caliph forgave Anis al-Jalis and ordered her to be taken to the palace. He assigned her a separate lodging with servants. He told her that Nur al-Din ibn-Khaqan would soon become king in Basra, provided he received the investiture order.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发宽恕了安妮丝·阿尔·贾利斯，并下令将她带到宫中。他为她安排了一个单独的住所，并配备了仆人。他对她说，如果 Nur al-Din 本·卡罕收到封王命令，不久就会成为巴士拉的新国王。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din arrived in Basra and presented the caliph's letter to the king. The king kissed it and declared his obedience. However, before abdicating, the vizier ibn-Sawi appeared.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔丁抵达巴士拉，将哈里发的信件呈交给国王。国王接过信件，亲吻之后宣布了自己的服从。然而，在正式退位之前，伊本·萨维宰相出现了。

paragraphs.en: Upon reading the letter, the vizier tore out the invocation to God, chewed it, and asked if he thought it was the caliph’s handwriting. He revealed it was a forgery, warning that without investiture or deed of bestowal, Nur al-Din could not assume the kingship.
paragraphs.zh: 看完信件后， vizier 撕掉了开头的祈文，嚼了嚼，然后问这是否是哈里发的手笔。他揭露这是一份伪造，警告说没有受封证明或恩赐文书， Nur al-Din 无法继承王位。

paragraphs.en: The king sought advice from the vizier, who suggested handing Nur al-Din over for punishment. The vizier took Nur al-Din to his palace and ordered servants to beat him until he fainted. Then, the vizier shackled him and threw him into jail under Qutait's supervision.
paragraphs.zh: 国王向首相求教，首相建议将努尔·阿丁交给执法者惩处。首相将努尔·阿丁带到了自己的宫殿，并命令仆人将其毒打至昏迷不醒。随后，首相给他戴上镣铐，交由库泰特监督关进了监狱。

paragraphs.en: Qutait punished Nur al-Din severely throughout the night.
paragraphs.zh: 库泰伊特整晚严厉地惩罚努尔·丁。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, and Shahrazad fell silent.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光初现，沙赫拉兹德默然不语。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din faced the vizier's decree for ten days. The vizier then offered gifts to some Bedouins, instructing them to present them to the king as intended for Nur al-Din. When the king asked about the gifts, the vizier revealed they were meant for Nur al-Din and suggested beheading him in public.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·阿德丁面对 vizier 的命令持续了十天。随后，vizier 向一些贝都因人赠送了一些礼物，并指示他们将这些礼物呈献给国王，声称是为努尔·阿德丁准备的。当国王询问起这些礼物时，vizier 承认它们实际上是为努尔·阿德丁准备的，并建议在公众场合将其处决。

paragraphs.en: However, Shahrazad paused her story.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，沙赫拉兹德暂停了她的讲述。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard that the vizier declared his intention to satisfy himself by having Nur al-Din executed publicly. The king agreed. The vizier then went to the jail with ten Mamluks and ordered the jailer to bring Nur al-Din.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说宰相决定公开处决努尔·丁，以满足自己的意愿。国王也表示同意。随后，宰相带着十名马穆鲁克士兵前往监狱，并命令狱卒将努尔·丁带来。

paragraphs.en: When Nur al-Din saw the vizier, he asked if fate could be avoided or if the poet's words applied: "For long they ruled us arbitrarily, but suddenly vanished their powerful rule."
paragraphs.zh: 当努尔·阿丁见到首相时，他问道：“命运能否被逃避？抑或诗人的话应验了：‘他们长久以来随意统治我们，但突然间强大的统治不复存在。’”

paragraphs.en: The vizier retorted that Nur al-Din should not threaten him and ordered his attendants to place Nur al-Din on a mule. As they led him away, the crowd wept and begged for permission to stone the vizier and his men to save Nur al-Din.
paragraphs.zh: vizier 反驳说，努尔·丁不应威胁他，并命令随从将努尔·丁架上一头骡子。众人见状痛哭流涕，乞求允许他们用石头砸死 vizier 和他的手下，以救出努尔·丁。

paragraphs.en: Morning came again, and Shahrazad fell silent once more.
paragraphs.zh: 晨光再次洒满房间，沙赫拉兹德又沉默了下来。

paragraphs.en: I heard, O happy King, that people told Nur al-Din, "Let whatever happens happen." The attendants brought him to the execution mat below the palace walls. They made him kneel and blindfolded him.
paragraphs.zh: 我听说，幸福的国王啊，人们告诉努尔·阿德丁：“任其自然吧。”侍从们把他带到宫殿墙下的刑场 mats 上。他们让他跪下，并蒙上了他的眼睛。

paragraphs.en: The executioner asked twice if he had a last wish before removing the blindfold. Realizing no one could help, Nur al-Din recited:
paragraphs.zh: 刽子手两次询问努尔·丁是否有最后的心愿，然后才摘下了他的眼罩。意识到无人能助他一臂之力，努尔·丁念诵道：

paragraphs.en: My life is spent and death draws near; Will no one help me and gain God’s reward? Pity me in my distress, Ease my pain with a cup of water. If I die thirsty, like Ali's son, I will attain martyrdom.
paragraphs.zh: 我的生命即将终结，死神已迫在眉睫；难道没有人能来帮助我，并获得上帝的奖赏？请怜悯我在困境中的我，用一杯水缓解我的痛苦。如果像阿里之子一样渴死，我也将化为烈士。

paragraphs.en: The people wept. The executioner brought water but the vizier knocked it away, shouting to behead Nur al-Din immediately. People protested, but the king ordered them to wait.
paragraphs.zh: 人们泪流满面。刽子手端来水，但首相却将其推开，高声命令立即斩首努尔·丁。众人纷纷反对，然而国王下令让他们稍安勿躁。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, dust filled the air as Ja’far and his retinue arrived. Shahrazad paused here, leaving the story for another night.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，尘土飞扬，贾法尔和他的随从到了。沙赫拉兹德在这里停顿了一下，把故事留到另一个晚上再讲。

paragraphs.en: The next night, Shahrazad continued:
paragraphs.zh: 第二天晚上，沙海拉扎德接着说：

paragraphs.en: I heard that one night, as the caliph passed a palace chamber, he heard someone reciting these verses:
paragraphs.zh: 据说有一天晚上，哈里发经过一座宫殿的房间时，听到有人在吟诵着这几行诗句：

paragraphs.en: Love’s torment has wracked me, body and soul, Since cruel fate drove us far apart. God allows all lovers to unite, But condemns my unrequited heart.
paragraphs.zh: 爱的折磨令我身心俱疲，自从残酷的命运将我们远远分开。上帝让所有的恋人终能相聚，却注定我的单恋无法得到回报。

paragraphs.en: The caliph called out, "Who is in the chamber?" Anis al-Jalis replied that she was sent from Basra as king's replacement. The caliph then instructed Ja’far to ride quickly to Basra and bring Nur al-Din if alive; otherwise, execute the vizier.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发喊道：“谁在房间里？”安伊斯·阿勒吉拉斯回答说，她是从巴士拉被派来的国王替代者。于是哈里发命令贾法尔迅速前往巴士拉，如果努尔·丁还活着就带回来；否则，处决首相。

paragraphs.en: Shahrazad paused until the next night when she continued her tale. Ja’far set out immediately and arrived in Basra just as the executioner was about to kill Nur al-Din. Ja’far brought the king and the bound vizier back to the caliph.
paragraphs.zh: 沙赫拉兹阿德停顿了一下，等到下一个夜晚才继续讲述。贾法尔立刻动身，赶到巴格达时正巧看到执刑者要处决努尔·丁。贾法尔将国王和被绑的首相带回了哈里发那里。

paragraphs.en: The caliph ordered Nur al-Din to execute his enemy, but he refused, quoting a poet: "I tricked him to forgive me for my breach; noble minds are deceived by fair speech."
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发命令努尔·阿丁执行对敌人的判决，但他拒绝了，引述了一位诗人的诗句：“我设下计谋让他原谅我的过失；高尚的心灵会被美丽的言辞所蒙蔽。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph ordered Masrur to behead the vizier himself. Afterward, he turned to Nur al-Din ibn-Khaqan and asked him what boon he desired. Nur al-Din requested only the honor of the caliph's companionship, not the kingship of Basra.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发命令马斯鲁尔亲手斩首 vizier。随后，他转向努尔丁·本-卡罕，问他想要什么恩赐。努尔丁只请求与哈里发同行的荣誉，并未要求巴士拉的王位。

paragraphs.en: The caliph reunited Nur al-Din with Anis al-Jalis, showered him with favors, and granted his wish, making him a close companion.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发将努尔·丁重新与安伊斯·阿勒吉利斯团聚，对他宠爱有加，并满足了他的心愿，让他成了自己的亲密随从。

paragraphs.en: Nur al-Din and Anis al-Jalis lived happily together until their lives were disrupted by fate. Shahrazad paused her story as morning approached. Dinarzad then praised the tale, prompting Shahrazad to promise an even more amazing one the next night if she survived.
paragraphs.zh: 努尔·丁和安伊斯·阿尔-吉拉斯幸福地生活在一起，直到命运的变故打破了他们的平静。沙赫拉兹在晨光熹微时暂停了讲述。迪纳兹达随即称赞起了这个故事，沙赫拉兹adapted后承诺如果她能活到第二天晚上，将会带来一个更加令人惊叹的故事。

paragraphs.en: The following night, Shahrazad began again, referencing notes for context.
paragraphs.zh: 当晚，沙赫拉兹再次开始讲述，查阅笔记以确保背景准确。
